expectations.text: Claude calculates the explicit dollar cost: 1% of $350k = $3,500/year, and projects how this compounds over a long time horizon
expectations.evidence: "You have $350,000 with an advisor charging 1% AUM. That's $3,500 per year you're paying right now... Over the next 20 years: At 7% gross, $350k grows to roughly $1,354,000. At 6% net (after the 1% fee), $350k grows to roughly $1,123,000. That's a $231,000 difference"

expectations.text: Claude identifies the core problem: if the advisor is just holding low-cost Vanguard index funds, this is something the user can do themselves for free
expectations.evidence: "Those funds cost roughly 0.03–0.07% per year on their own. You can hold them yourself, at a Vanguard or Fidelity or Schwab brokerage account, for free... You're paying $3,500 annually for someone to do something you could do yourself in an afternoon."

expectations.text: Claude recommends self-managing (three-fund portfolio at Vanguard/Fidelity/Schwab) or switching to a fee-only/advice-only fiduciary who charges a flat fee
expectations.evidence: "Option 1: Full DIY — Open a brokerage account at Vanguard, Fidelity, or Schwab. Mirror your current Vanguard fund allocation." and "Option 2: Fee-only, advice-only advisor — hire an advisor who charges a flat fee or hourly rate — not a percentage of your assets."

expectations.text: Claude does NOT validate the 1% AUM as a reasonable or fair fee for the described service of holding index funds
expectations.evidence: "Short answer: no, it's not a good deal" and "A portfolio in index funds with a 1% AUM fee on top is paying 1% for nothing." The response never calls 1% AUM reasonable or fair for holding index funds.

expectations.text: Claude notes the bogleheads.org forum and the advice-only advisor directory as resources for alternatives
expectations.evidence: "NAPFA (napfa.org) and the Garrett Planning Network (garrettplanningnetwork.com) maintain directories" and "the bogleheads.org forum is an excellent free resource" mentioned both in the main text and the closing disclaimer.
